A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FS-DFM and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Corresponding content can be matched across the redesign, including v1 Table 5 becoming v2 Table 6.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model evaluations, component ablations, synthetic checkerboard simulations, and generated examples in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds MAUVE measurements and an expanded comparison with other diffusion models.

M1.justification: Step-size conditioning, cumulative-scalar updates, RK-2/RK-4 EMA teachers, blended training losses, architecture, and jump sampling remain unchanged. The added Bregman-divergence attribution explains the existing loss rather than introducing a different objective.

E1.justification: Both versions retain FineWeb-Edu training, WikiText-103 evaluation, 1024-token generation and corruption recovery, 512-token-prefix continuation, and the checkerboard demonstration. The expanded baseline comparison does not document an additional benchmark or task.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained DFM, LLaDA, and Dream comparisons, v2 Table 5 adds SDTT at four refinement depths, two HDLM configurations, MDLM–OWT, SEDD, and four ReMDM variants. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator families. FS-DLM labels in existing tables are corrected to FS-DFM.

E3.justification: v2 adds MAUVE to the continuation evaluation and specifies an eight-step sampling budget for the expanded comparison, including different SDTT round counts and HDLM configurations. Existing preprocessing, training budgets, and the 512-prefix/512-continuation protocol remain unchanged as documented.

E4.justification: The original scalar, solver, step-size-policy, and source-distribution ablations and qualitative cases are retained. New Appendix E.3/Table 5 adds a limited refinement-depth analysis: SDTT perplexity decreases from 612.38 at one round to 131.71 at seven rounds, informing whether additional refinement closes the reported gap.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. New table entries continue point-estimate reporting, and the existing graphical displays are retained.

E6.justification: v2 adds MAUVE scores and results for the new comparator families, while revising existing rows. In Table 2, eight-step FS-DFM 1.7B perplexity changes from 76.04 to 72.84. Across v1 Table 5 and v2 Table 6, one-step Dream-I changes from 24401.02 to 46371 and LLaDA-I from 13866.24 to 8677. These are substantive numerical revisions under unchanged stated continuation settings.

T1.justification: The CTMC definitions, Proposition A.1, Kolmogorov equations, jump-process derivations, cumulative-scalar mathematics, and losses are retained. Equation renumbering, identifying z as a token sequence, and attributing the existing loss to Bregman divergence introduce no new formal result or mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central novelty and performance claims: few-step discrete flow matching for long-horizon language modeling, matching a similar-size 1024-step DFM in eight steps for 1024-token generation, with up to 128-fold faster sampling.

C2.justification: Appendix E.3 adds comparison-specific explanations linking the advantage over SDTT to learned finite-step dynamics and interpreting the expanded results as evidence of training-token efficiency. Appendix D newly identifies hybrid mask/uniform sources as unexplored. Existing ablation interpretations and broader task limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an explicit code address on the first page, replacing the abstract's release promise and removing the standalone reproducibility statement. Table 5 adds comparator sizes, training-token counts, and configuration labels. Core implementation and hardware details remain unchanged; checkpoint release is still described as planned in Appendix D.

R1.justification: New Appendix E.3 substantially expands positioning against self-distillation, hybrid diffusion, and masked/remasking approaches, emphasizing finite-step dynamics and training efficiency. It adds discussion and citations for HDLM, MDLM, SEDD, and ReMDM, alongside new MAUVE and flow-matching-loss references. Section 2 is largely retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are preserved. Changes include title and model-label corrections, brief denoiser explanations, insertion of Appendix E.3, corresponding appendix renumbering, and removal of the standalone reproducibility paragraph. The existing narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a document-wide Apple layout with a new title panel, typography, margins, colored links, and resized or relocated figures. Tables 2 and 6 gain MAUVE columns and entropy highlighting, and a new grouped baseline table is added. All nine figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: MAUVE measurements and comparisons with relevant few-step competitors make v2's evaluation more informative, while the explicit code address improves access information. These gains are limited by unexplained revisions to existing scores and Appendix E.3's claim to isolate data-scale effects despite Table 5 reporting additional FS-DFM fine-tuning tokens. The central method and supporting ablations remain unchanged.
